\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Invariance — Sequence}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.Sequence
\section{Overview}
A sequence of hybrid input families gives the summed replacement bound. Equality of independent coordinate laws also determines the joint vector law.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Selection from two coordinate copies]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridIndex}
\leanok
For integers $n,r\ge0$ and an index $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the hybrid selection chooses the right copy of $i$ if $i<r$ and the left copy otherwise, as an element of two disjoint copies of the coordinate set.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hybrid family after initial replacements]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridIndex}
Let $Z_{L,i},Z_{R,i}\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be two indexed families, $0\le i<n$, and let $r\ge0$ be an integer. The hybrid family $H^{(r)}$ has $H^{(r)}_i=Z_{R,i}$ for $i<r$ and $H^{(r)}_i=Z_{L,i}$ for $i\ge r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Injectivity of hybrid coordinate selection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridIndex_injective}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridIndex}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $n$ and $r$, the map from the $n$-coordinate set to the disjoint
union of two copies of that set, sending $i$ to the right copy when $i<r$ and to the
left copy otherwise, is injective.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Initial hybrid equals the left family]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridIndex, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\Omega$ be a set, and let
$Z_{L,i},Z_{R,i}:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be two families indexed by $0\le i<n$. For the
hybrid family that uses $Z_{R,i}$ when $i<r$ and $Z_{L,i}$ otherwise, its value at $r=0$
is $Z_{L,i}$ for every coordinate $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The final hybrid is the right family]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput_all}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridIndex, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\Omega$ be a type, and let $Z$ assign a real-valued
function on $\Omega$ to each element of the disjoint union of two copies of the
$n$-coordinate set. The hybrid family at stage $n$ equals the family whose coordinate
$i$ is the function assigned by $Z$ to the right copy of $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Consecutive hybrids agree off the changed coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput_succ_off}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridIndex, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\Omega$ be a type, let $Z$ assign a real-valued
function on $\Omega$ to each element of the disjoint union of two copies of the
$n$-coordinate set, and let $i,j$ be coordinates with $j\ne i$. The hybrid families at
stages $i$ and $i+1$ have the same function at coordinate $j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth-derivative invariance bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_of_independent_pair}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridIndex, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridIndex_injective, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput_succ_off, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybrid_expectation_bound, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.single_coordinate_replacement_bound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.eval_supported, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
\proofsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p033-b002}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$ be a
multilinear coefficient family on $n$ coordinates of degree at most $k$. Suppose the
$2n$ real random variables $Z_{L,i},Z_{R,i}$ are mutually independent and each satisfies
the invariance moment conditions: its mean and third moment are zero, its second moment
is one, and its fourth moment is at most $9$, with finite fourth moment. If $\psi\in
C^4(\mathbb R)$ and $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}|$ everywhere, then
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(Z_L))-\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(Z_R))\right|\le \frac
C{12}\,9^k\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{Inf}_i[F]^2,
\]
where $F(Z)(\omega)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(\omega)$ and
$\mathrm{Inf}_i[F]$ is the influence of the Walsh-basis function defined by the same
coefficients.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Joint laws from independent coordinate laws]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.identDistrib_of_independent_coordinates}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be measurable
probability spaces, and let $X_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $Y_i:\Xi\to\mathbb R$ be
coordinate families. If each family is independent and corresponding coordinates have
the same distribution, then the random vectors $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ and $(Y_i)_{i\in I}$
have the same distribution.
\end{theorem}

\section{Additional declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Hybrid expectation bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybrid_expectation_bound}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybrid_expectation_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput_all, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.hybridInput_zero, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $F$ be a
real coefficient family on the subsets of the $n$ coordinates, and let $Z$ be two
families of real-valued functions on $\Omega$, indexed by those coordinates. Let
$\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $B_i\in\mathbb R$ for each coordinate $i$. If, for each
$i$, the absolute difference between the integrals of $\psi$ applied to the multilinear
evaluations at hybrids $i$ and $i+1$ is at most $B_i$, then the absolute difference
between the corresponding integrals for the all-left and all-right families is at most
$\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}B_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Independent coupling of two input families]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.independent_input_coupling}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.independent_input_coupling}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\iota$ be a finite index set, and let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability
spaces. Suppose $X_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $Y_i:\Xi\to\mathbb R$ are measurable up to
null sets for every $i\in\iota$. There exist a probability space carrying a mutually
independent family $(Z_j)_{j\in\iota\sqcup\iota}$ such that each $Z_{\mathrm{inl}(i)}$
has the same distribution as $X_i$ under $\mu$, and each $Z_{\mathrm{inr}(i)}$ has the
same distribution as $Y_i$ under $\nu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Identical laws of multilinear evaluations]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.identDistrib_evalMultilinearRV}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.identDistrib_evalMultilinearRV}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.identDistrib_of_independent_coordinates, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability
spaces, and let $F$ be a real coefficient family on subsets of the $n$ coordinates.
Suppose the coordinate families $X_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $Y_i:\Xi\to\mathbb R$ are
each independent, and that $X_i$ and $Y_i$ have the same distribution for every
coordinate $i$. Then the multilinear evaluations $\sum_S F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ and
$\sum_S F(S)\prod_{i\in S}Y_i$ have the same distribution under $\mu$ and $\nu$,
respectively.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Independent coupling preserving polynomial distributions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.independent_polynomial_coupling}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.independent_polynomial_coupling}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.identDistrib_evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.independent_input_coupling, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $F$ assign a real coefficient to every subset of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let
$X_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $Y_i:\Xi\to\mathbb R$ be measurable up to null sets.
Suppose the family $(X_i)_{i<n}$ is mutually independent under $\mu$, and $(Y_i)_{i<n}$
is mutually independent under $\nu$. There exist a probability space carrying a mutually
independent family $(Z_j)_{j\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)\sqcup\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ whose left and
right coordinates have the respective distributions of $X_i$ and $Y_i$, and such that
evaluating $F$ on each coordinate family gives, respectively, the same distributions as
evaluating it on $X$ under $\mu$ and on $Y$ under $\nu$.
\end{theorem}
